proposed_widenings.name: spellcasting_grant
proposed_widenings.justification: Pact Magic is not an activated feature with a discrete effect — it is a persistent spellcasting framework. It grants cantrips, a spell slot pool (with pact-specific rules: all slots same level, count+level both scale by class level), and a prepared spell list. No existing ClassFeatureMechanics family models a spellcasting grant. The activation family requires a ClassFeatureEffect (grant_extra_action | heal_hp), neither of which is applicable.
proposed_widenings.evidence: Through occult ceremony, you have formed a pact with a mysterious entity to gain magical powers... the ability to cast spells. / Spell Slots. The Warlock Features table shows how many spell slots you have to cast your Warlock spells of levels 1–5. The table also shows the level of those slots, all of which are the same level. You regain all expended Pact Magic spell slots when you finish a Short or Long Rest.

proposed_widenings.name: grant_spell_access
proposed_widenings.justification: ClassFeatureEffect needs a variant to represent granting a spell list (cantrips + prepared spells) with counts that scale by class level. This is mechanically distinct from grant_extra_action and heal_hp, and is needed for all spellcasting class features (Bard Spellcasting, Cleric Spellcasting, etc.).
proposed_widenings.evidence: Cantrips. You know two Warlock cantrips of your choice. / Prepared Spells of Level 1+. You prepare the list of level 1+ spells that are available for you to cast with this feature. To start, choose two level 1 Warlock spells.

proposed_widenings.name: pact_magic_slot_pool
proposed_widenings.justification: The Pact Magic slot pool has two co-scaling dimensions (slot count AND slot level, both indexed by class level), all slots at the same level. This is not representable as a use_count resource cap (which only scales one scalar value). A dedicated slot-pool resource shape is needed that encodes both dimensions via threshold_tiers on the class axis.
proposed_widenings.evidence: The Warlock Features table shows how many spell slots you have to cast your Warlock spells of levels 1–5. The table also shows the level of those slots, all of which are the same level.

notes: All spellcasting features (bard_spellcasting_l1, cleric_spellcasting_l1, druid_spellcasting_l1, ranger_spellcasting_l1, etc.) face the same structural gap — the class-feature surface has no spellcasting-grant family. Pact Magic adds a second layer of pressure: its slot system is mechanically distinct from standard prepared-spellcasting (all slots same level, short-rest recovery), so even a generic spellcasting family would need a pact_magic variant. No dhall or trace produced.
